answer: I'd like to describe a photograph that I look at almost every day. A photograph I treasure is one of my entire extended family gathered together at a reunion several years ago. It was taken during Eid in the courtyard of my grandparents' home in the village, with everyone squeezed onto a few plastic chairs and a mat on the ground. My grandparents are sitting in the middle, surrounded by their children and grandchildren, and a couple of neighbours who wandered in at the last minute. It captures a rare moment when everyone, across three generations, was in the same place at the same time. It was taken by my cousin, who had just bought his first proper camera and insisted on setting a timer so he could run into the frame himself. In fact, you can just about see him mid-jump, still trying to reach his spot. What makes it so [[precious]] is that some of the older relatives in it, like my great-uncle, have since passed away. Whenever I look at it, I am filled with a warm sense of [[nostalgia]]. The photo is not technically perfect; it is slightly blurry and someone is looking the wrong way, but that only [[adds to its charm]]. What I love is how it froze a genuinely happy, [[fleeting]] moment forever. It reminds me of the importance of family and how quickly time passes. Honestly, no professionally staged photograph could ever mean as much to me. I keep a printed copy framed on my wall, and it never fails to make me smile. It is a powerful reminder of how [[irreplaceable]] these moments and people are.

followUps.q: Do you take many photographs yourself?
followUps.answer: Quite a few, but mostly on my phone, and I rarely print them. I'd like to change that, because a printed photo somehow feels more permanent than thousands of images [[buried in]] a phone gallery.

followUps.q: Would you like to take a similar photo in the future?
followUps.answer: Yes, very much. I'd love to organise another family photo at my grandparents' home next Eid, especially now that my sister's children are old enough to sit still, or at least try.

note: Set the photo at Eid in the grandparents' village home with grandparents alive and present (only a great-uncle has passed away); added who took it (cousin with a timer); new mark 'adds to its charm'.
